title: Robust and cost-effective computational methods for haplotype-resolved genome assemblies
text:
De no!ID haplotype-resolved genome assembly is the most comprehensive solution to understand genomic sequences. This
proposal aims to develop cost-effective computational methods for high-quality haplotype-resolved assemblies by utilizing
multiple sequencing technologies. The new assembly algorijhms in this proposal not only could be used by large-scale
sequencing consortiums such as the Human Pangenome Reference Consortium (HPRC) and the Genome in a Bottle (GIAB),
but also could pave the way to personal genome assembly for genomic research and clinical applications.

title: Ferroptosis in knock-in sepiapterin reductase mutation rabbits
text:
This proposal investigates the mechanisms of motor deficits of cerebral palsy and congenital
tetrahydrobiopterin deficiency, which involve formation of destructive reactive chemical species in early brain
injury resulting in cell death. New information about which forms of cell death, how they affect brain cells, and
how effective potential therapies are in an animal model of cerebral palsy will be very valuable for future drug
development in human studies.

title: Molecular analysis of bacterial interactions
text:
Microbial interactions play key roles in maintenance of diverse ecosystems and imbalance in
microbial community structure negatively impacts human health. Understanding of microbial
mechanisms underlying their ability to sense and respond to competition as well as alliance will
allow researchers to engineer these abilities to promote health. By using innovative and
multidisciplinary approaches, we will identify and discovery new natural products that mediate
niche-specific microbial interactions at the molecular, genomic, and gene expression level.

title: The development of a flexible carbon fiber penetrating nerve cuff and cortical array for neural recording, stimulation, and neurochemical detection
text:
Penetrating electrodes greatly enhance our ability to study and interact with neurological structures underlying
many mental health and other neurological disorders. However, there is a critical need for improved neural
interfaces that are suited for chronic implantation to support the development and clinical translation of devices
to treat neurological conditions such as drug-resistant depression, anxiety, and drug abuse. Spike Neuro and
the University of Michigan are partnering together to develop a flexible, 3D, carbon fiber penetrating array for
electrophysiology applications in complex and fragile biological systems with excellent biocompatibility, chronic
performance, and potential for clinical translation.

title: Distributed cortical feedback mechanisms for context-dependent auditory processing
text:
The auditory cortex receives widespread feedback from higher-order cortical areas that likely govern how
sounds are interpreted and used for behavior, yet their collective influence has never been systematically
compared. This project uses a newly developed, high-density cortical inactivation approach to test how each of
these regions modulates auditory cortical responses during passive listening and during an auditory decision-
making task. By defining how these distributed pathways jointly shape sensory representations, the work will
provide the first integrated account of cortical feedback organization in the auditory system.

title: Simultaneous MRI/US for real-time liver ablation guidance and confirmation
text:
Current approaches to guiding percutaneous liver ablation have significant limitations yielding poor tumor
control rates. This multi-disciplinary, multi-institutional Academic Industrial Partnership will develop and
validate a simultaneous US and MR solution in combination with advanced MR methods for real-time
guidance, treatment monitoring and margin assessment during liver ablations with the ultimate goal of
improving patient outcomes.

title: Identifying the effects of NRF2 signaling on lung squamous cell carcinoma development
text:
Human lung squamous cell carcinomas remain one of the most common cancers worldwide with dismal
prognoses and limited therapies. During the past eight years, we have focused on understanding how changes
in the NFE2L2 (NRF2) signaling pathway in these cancers make them more aggressive with poorer patient
survival. In this application, we will develop a new mouse model for lung squamous cell cancers to identify how
NRF signaling changes the onset and growth of this cancer and alters the tumor’s response to immunotherapy
treatments such as nivolumab (Opdivo) and pembrolizumab (Keytruda).

title: Chemistry-Biology Interface Predoctoral Training Program
text:
Training graduate students for careers following attainment of the Ph.D. is one of the central missions of
academic institutions. This grant is centered on training and education of Ph.D. scientists for careers that
require knowledge at the interface of chemistry and biology. Since so much of biomedical research requires
interdisciplinary knowledge, we view training at this junction to comprise a fundamentally important area for
several different fields including academic research, the pharmaceutical industry, and non-traditional careers in
science.

title: Center for Molecular Imaging Technology & Translation (CMITT)
text:
Project Narrative for the Center for Molecular Imaging Technology and Translation (CMITT)
The Center for Molecular Imaging Technology and Translation (CMITT) is a National Center for Biomedical
Imaging and Bioengineering located within the Gordon Center for Medical Imaging at the Massachusetts General
Hospital. CMITT advances the methodology of PET/MR and covers the entire range of radiochemistry/radiopharmacy
to image formation and processing including tomographic reconstruction and estimation/quantitation, paving the way
for research applications and clinical translation.

title: Molecular Screening Shared Resource (MSSR)
text: MOLECULAR SCREENING SHARED RESOURCE (MSSR) ABSTRACT The UCLA Jonsson Comprehensive Cancer Center (JCCC) Molecular Screening Shared Resource (MSSR) objective is to provide transformative high throughput screening (HTS) for small and large molecules to the JCCC research community. This objective is achieved through three Specific Aims: (1) To expand screening capabilities with state-of-the-art approaches; (2) To expand functional genomics screening capabilities; and (3) To enhance drug development capabilities. MSSR offers a comprehensive array of HTS services enabling JCCC investigators to discover new molecular targets, identify agents for these targets, and characterize and optimize agents for translation. Established in 2003, MSSR and has grown from 950 to 3,600 sq. ft. of BSL2+ space. From 2019 – 2023, 43 JCCC investigators used MSSR accounting for 41% of total usage. Of JCCC member usage, 66% was by peer-review funded investigators. MSSR services, including assay development, HTS, data analyses, and follow-up, such as potency, toxicity, and selective testing, for both small and large molecular drugs, contributed to 50 cancer-relevant publications with 42% in high impact (IF ≥10) journals. MSSR offers access to >300K compounds in multiple libraries for chemical genomics, repurposing, and drug discovery. MSSR also offers a wide array of functional genomics libraries, such as >60K human lentiviral CRISPR gRNAs, shRNA lentiviral constructs, siRNAs covering druggable mouse and human genomes, and a genome wide lentiviral and transfection ready cDNA library. Projects are supported by three expert MSSR scientists on six fully automated, robotic screening systems, one new since 2019, with a daily capacity >100K samples. All plate reader assays and plate formats are addressable with ≥1,536-well plates, as are advanced assay readouts including confocal spinning disk microscopy. MSSR uses a collaborative model integrating users into a project team consisting of the JCCC investigator, MSSR leadership, and MSSR scientists. This approach brings in expert and often nuanced knowledge while keeping MSSR headcount and associated costs low but scalable with demand. Moreover, this provides an excellent educational opportunity, with 204 students learning in one-on-one training from MSSR experts since 2019. MSSR provides workshops on assay development, AI based image analysis, and data mining. All projects advance using industry best practices including generation of standard operating procedures (SOPs) and milestone driven project management. MSSR Director Robert Damoiseaux, PhD (CSCB) is an international expert in HTS with industry background. Damoiseaux guides each project, ensuring research excellence. MSSR management is overseen by JCCC Associate Director for Shared Resources, Zoran Galic, PhD (TII), with additional support and guidance from a five member MSSR Faculty Advisory Committee (FAC), comprised entirely of JCCC members. Examples of MSSR impact include the first MSSR small molecule agent, TRE-515, passing a Phase I dosing trial in 2023, and the first large molecule MSSR drug, DUNP19, entering cGMP production to prepare for clinical trials after receiving FDA orphan drug designation in 2022.

title: Phospho- and natural-variant regulation of heterotrimeric G protein signaling
text:
Many human infectious and genetic diseases disrupt G protein pathways, which constitute a conserved
eukaryotic signaling mechanism. The proposed research will employ a highly tractable system to provide a
comprehensive understanding of the regulation of heterotrimeric G protein biochemistry and signaling by
subunit phosphorylation and natural variation in G protein sequence, and will thus identify specific regulatory
paradigms that strengthen or impair the G protein cycle, heterotrimer interactions, subcellular localization, and
coupling with other proteins. Results obtained will identify new G protein conformations for therapeutics, and
will distinguish disruptive and benign natural variants, thereby identifying conditions and opportunities wherein
targeted interventions should and can be prioritized to repair dysregulated aspects of G protein signaling while
simultaneously avoiding impairment of other G protein functions and phenotypes.

title: Advancing Antimicrobial Use Measurement in U.S. Companion Animal Practice
text:
Improved understanding of antimicrobial usage patterns in companion animals is needed to support efforts
to mitigate antimicrobial resistance—a growing global health threat. The project will provide actionable
targets for antimicrobial stewardship by 1) harnessing data from the Companion Animal Veterinary
Surveillance Network, a successful public-private partnership that collects, standardizes, and analyzes
veterinary electronic health data from over 1,300 U.S. clinics and 2) performing targeted point-prevalence
surveys of antimicrobial use in dogs, cats, and horses. The findings could inform evidence-based policy
changes and strengthen surveillance systems, ultimately enhancing public health outcomes.

title: Development and Validation of Orthotopic Oncopig Glioma Models for Preclinical Locoregional Therapeutic Evaluation
text:
Glioblastoma (GBM), one of the most common and aggressive forms of brain cancer,
remains incurable with a median survival of less than 2 years, highlighting the need for improved GBM treatment
strategies. Advances in GBM treatments are highly dependent on the development of new systems to better
understand cancer progression and treatment responses. The aim of this innovative proposal is to validate
genetically defined, immunocompetent pig allo- and xenograft GBM models for preclinical therapeutic evaluation,
with the overall goal of providing large animal GBM models and preclinical testing services to device and
pharmaceutical companies.

title: Improving Patient Care through Respectful Medical Record Language
text: Medical records are an integral method of communicating about patients and yet the language clinicians use in clinical notes may reflect respect or disrespect towards patients, which may in tern impact the care patients receive. The specific aims of this proposal are to develop a taxonomy of language in medical records, to measure use of positive and negative language in medical records using natural language processing (NLP), and then to increase respect in healthcare environments using proven implementation science (IS) strategies. Because language may have a powerful role in influencing subsequent clinician attitudes and behavior, this project could have a large impact on the promotion of respect for all patients.

title: Dissecting the Role of Ca2+ Channel Dysfunction in the Pathogenesis of Neurodevelopmental Disorders
text:
Multiple mutations within the CaV1.2 calcium channel have been shown to cause a neurodevelopmental disorder
(NDD) including symptoms overlapping with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). The mutations cause an excess
of calcium entry through the channel, which impacts neuronal excitability, calcium signaling and protein
expression. Because disrupted calcium dynamics may be a common feature in a larger subset of NDD, studying
the impact of these CaV1.2 mutations on neuronal function will help us understand the role of calcium signaling
in NDD.

title: Visinin-like protein-1 modulation of nicotinic receptors
text:
NARRATIVE. Tobacco use is the leading cause of preventable death in the United States. This application will
determine for the first time how visinin-like protein-1 (an endogenous protein found in the brain) modulates the
function and expression of the most abundant neuronally-expressed nicotinic receptor subtype, which is well
known to play a pivotal role in nicotine use disorder. By addressing critical gaps in our knowledge, this research
will 1) advance the scientific understanding of intrinsic control mechanisms regulating nicotinic receptor function
and expression, and 2) may provide an essential foundation for the development of new therapies to promote
nicotine use cessation.

title: CTSA Postdoctoral T32 at University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences
text:
We propose a new T32 Postdoctoral Training Program focused on Health Sciences Innovation and
Entrepreneurship (HSIE) Training Program, which will offer mentored research training to postdoctoral fellows
in the Colleges of Medicine, Nursing, Pharmacy and Public Health. This inter-professional training will be
coupled to didactic and experiential learning to equip trainees with the skillset to catalyze research discoveries
into health care applications. Program graduates will be uniquely positioned as translational scientists to
succeed as academic investigators or pursue other exciting career options that depend on scientific and
operation principles of the translation process.

title: Reverse Engineering of Cell Senescence
text:
Researchers have discovered new types of cells, called “senescent cells”, that are suspected to
be involved in aging. We plan to use novel technologies we developed to find out how these
cells develop, how they damage normal tissues, and how to kill them.

title: Nebraska Center for Integrated Biomolecular Communication (NCIBC)
text:
Diseases result when the internal stability and normal communications within and among biological pathways
are disrupted by genetic defects, environmental disturbances, or pathogens. The Nebraska Center for Integrated
Biomolecular Communication (NCIBC) serves as a natural mixing chamber to integrate the research activities of
chemists, biochemists, engineers, and bioinformaticians to address critical knowledge gaps in our understanding
of how cells communicate and integrate metabolic and regulatory pathways relevant to disease development
and progression. NCIBC investigators will continue to bring together unique expertise in understanding complex
diseases and developing novel methodologies and technologies to probe communication pathways.

title: Investigating and targeting the translational landscape of DBA
text:
In humans, mutations in a number of core ribosome components lead to ribosomopathies, including Diamond-
Blackfan anemia (DBA), which is characterized by fatal bone marrow failure. In all of these cases, the
mechanism(s) that would account for cell type specific changes in hematopoietic cells underlying these
diseases remain poorly understood. Here, we propose to employ novel technologies to pinpoint how alterations
in accurate control of translation causes bone marrow failure in these diseases and identify small molecules
that activate translational control as a new targeted therapy for DBA.
